subject: language_arts

unit.title: Word classes & sentence types
unit.essentialQuestion: What jobs do words do, and how do sentences come in different types?

title: Nouns, adjectives and verbs (word jobs)
objectives: By the end, I can spot whether a word is a noun, an adjective or a verb.

vocabulary.definition: a naming word — a person, place or thing
a describing word — it tells you more about a noun

vocabulary.example: run, jump — and quiet ones like is and are

emphasize: Every word has a JOB, and three quick TESTS find it: 'the' in front → noun; 'I am ___ing' / can I do it → verb; describes a noun → adjective.
Verbs are doing OR BEING words — is, are, was are verbs too. 'The cat IS fluffy' — is is the verb.
Pre-empt calling everything a noun: run the test, don't guess.

keyConcepts: verb = doing or being word ('I am ___ing' test; is/are count)
misconceptions: calling everything a noun (guessing without a test)
verb = doing word only — missing being verbs (is/are/was)
muddling adjective and verb ('happy' called the doing word)
hooks: You're a word detective with three tools — every word in the room gets a job.
priorKnowledge: can read a simple sentence fluently (Year 1)

video.title: Noun Song from Grammaropolis - "Noun Town"
video.watchTask: Every time the song names a person, a place or a thing, whisper 'NOUN!' — count how many you catch.

afterCheck.question: What three kinds of things do nouns name?

plan.goal: Frame the lesson as 'word detective' with three tools; retrieve fluent sentence reading.
plan.note: Fast and playful — the detective frame carries the whole lesson. Show the three columns straight away.
plan.successCriteria: Child reads 'The happy dog ran.' fluently and is keen to 'hand out the jobs'.

script.say: Every single word has a JOB. Some words NAME things — dog, school — those are nouns. Some words DESCRIBE — fluffy, red — adjectives. Some words DO things — run, jump — verbs. Today you're a word detective, and I'm giving you three tools to find out each word's job. Detective badge on! First, read me this sentence: The happy dog ran.
script.adaptHints: Swap the example nouns for the child's interests (their pet, their favourite place). If the read is shaky, beat-read the tricky word first, then re-read smoothly.

blocks.caption: Word detective: every word has a job!

stuckProtocol: If the sentence read is shaky: beat-read any tricky word first (h-a-ppy), then re-read the whole sentence smoothly before moving on.

plan.goal: Model the three detective tools on dog / run / fluffy, then ball / jump / red — and reveal the quiet being verbs (is, are).
plan.note: Say which TOOL proved each word every time — the tests make abstract labels concrete. The being-verb reveal pre-empts the 'verbs only DO' trap.
plan.successCriteria: Child hears each test used aloud and sees six words land in the right columns, including 'is' named as a verb.

script.say: Three detective tools. Tool one, for NOUNS: can I put 'the' in front? The dog — yes! Dog is a noun. Tool two, for VERBS: can I DO it, or say 'I am ___ing'? I am running — yes! Run is a verb. Tool three, for ADJECTIVES: does it describe a noun? Fluffy — a fluffy dog — yes, it describes! Watch me test ball: 'the ball' works, so it's a noun. Jump: 'I am jumping' — verb. Red: 'a red ball' — it describes, adjective. And here's a detective secret: some verbs are quiet BEING words — is, are, was. 'The cat IS fluffy' — nobody is running or jumping, but 'is' is still the verb!
script.adaptHints: Keep the tool names identical every time ('the' test, 'I am ___ing' test, describes test). Act out the doing verbs; whisper the being verbs like a secret.

rows: Can I do it? 'I am ___ing' — or a being word: is, are

plan.goal: Shared detecting: child tests and sorts school, sleep, happy using the prompt for each tool.
plan.note: The character starts each test, the child finishes it. Insist on hearing WHICH tool proved it.
plan.successCriteria: Child sorts school → noun, sleep → verb, happy → adjective, saying the test aloud for each.

script.say: Detect with me. Take 'school'. Can I put 'the' in front? The school — yes! So it's a…? Now 'sleep' — can I do it? I am sleeping? Yes, so…? And 'happy' — does it describe? A happy cat — so…? Drag each word into its column, and tell me which tool proved it.
script.adaptHints: If the child answers without a test, ask 'which tool proved it?' before accepting. Swap 'a happy cat' for the child's pet.

blocks.prompt: Sort each word into its job — say the test out loud first!

check.question: Which tool proves 'school' is a noun?
check.expectedAnswer: The 'the' test — 'the school' works, so it's a noun.

wrongAnswers.why: reached for the verb tool first
wrongAnswers.remedy: Try it: 'I am schooling…' — sounds odd! Now try the other tool: can you put 'the' in front? 'The school' — which job does that prove?
Does 'school' describe another word, or does it NAME a place? Try 'a school dog'… no. Try 'the school' — yes! So it's a…?

plan.goal: Key diagnostic: find the verb in 'The happy dog ran.' — then probe which test proved it.
plan.note: 'dog' means noun/verb confusion; 'happy' means adjective/verb confusion. Always probe the test after a correct answer.
plan.successCriteria: Child picks 'ran' AND says the test that proved it (a doing word — 'I am running').

script.say: Detective challenge! Here's a whole sentence: The happy dog ran. Which word is the VERB? Use your tools… and be ready to tell me which tool proved it.
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'Which test proved it?' If the child is quick, ask for the noun and the adjective in the same sentence as a bonus.

blocks.prompt: Which word is the verb: The happy dog ran?
blocks.explain: You can DO it — 'I am running' works. Ran is the doing word, the verb.

check.question: Which word is the verb: 'The happy dog ran'?
check.expectedAnswer: ran (it's a doing word — 'I am running' works)

wrongAnswers.remedy: Can you DO a dog? No — but you can put 'the' before it, so dog is a noun. Which word is the DOING word?
Does 'happy' describe the dog? Yes — that's an adjective's job. Which word tells you what the dog DID?

plan.goal: Independent detecting: sort words into nouns/adjectives/verbs, including a being verb; say the test aloud each time.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Watch for: calling everything a noun; guessing without a test; muddling adjective and verb; missing is/are as verbs.
plan.successCriteria: Child sorts at least six words correctly using the tests, including one being verb.

script.say: Your case, detective! I'll hand you words — you run the tests and give each one its job. Say the test out loud every time, so I can hear your detective brain working.
script.adaptHints: Frame the word cards around the child's interests (their pet, football, dinosaurs) — the tests never change.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'Let's run the tests in order.'
Step down: two columns first (nouns vs verbs) — add adjectives back when secure.
ONE hint: 'Try putting the in front — does it work?'
Re-ask a smaller version: one single card.
Keep it safe: 'Detectives use their tools — let's test it together.'

plan.goal: Child states the three tests from memory; end on a win with process praise.
plan.note: Child-led; the character listens. Sneak in the being-verb secret one more time.
plan.successCriteria: Child recites: 'the' in front → noun; can do it / 'I am ___ing' → verb; describes a noun → adjective — and remembers is/are are verbs.

script.say: Case closed! Tell me your three detective tools for finding a word's job… And the secret one: is 'is' a verb? … Yes — a quiet being verb! You used a test on every word instead of guessing — that's how a real word detective works.
script.adaptHints: Praise the observed process: running a test before answering, saying tests aloud. Never 'clever' — always the strategy.

block.prompt: Two columns to start: is each word a NAMING word or a DOING word?

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Nouns: dog, ball · Verbs: run, jump

wrongAnswers.remedy: Run the verb tool: 'I am running' — does it work? Then which column?

wrongAnswers.why: thinks of throwing a ball, so calls it a doing word
wrongAnswers.remedy: You DO things with a ball, but can you say 'I am balling'? Try the other tool: 'the ball' — which job does that prove?

hints: If 'I am ___ing' works, it's a verb.

reteach.say: Two tools, two columns. 'The dog' works → noun column. 'I am running' works → verb column. Test, then sort — never guess.

practiceBank.skill: use the 'the' test to spot a noun

block.prompt: Which word passes the noun test — 'the ___' sounds right?
block.explain: 'The ball' sounds right — ball names a thing, so it's a noun. 'The jump'… tricky, but 'the fluffy' and 'the ran' definitely fail!

wrongAnswers.remedy: Say it aloud: 'the fluffy…' — the fluffy WHAT? It's waiting for a noun to describe. Which word names a thing all by itself?
'The ran' — does that sound right? Ran is what someone DID. Which word can you put 'the' before?

hints: Say 'the' before each word out loud.
A noun NAMES a thing — which word is a thing you could hold?

reteach.say: The 'the' test never lies. The ball — lovely, that's a thing, a noun. The fluffy — nope, fluffy is waiting to describe something. The ran — nope, ran is a doing word. Only naming words like 'the' in front.

block.emojis: ✅ the ball · ❌ the fluffy · ❌ the ran
block.caption: Only nouns pass the 'the' test

practiceBank.skill: sort words into all three classes

block.prompt: All three tools out! Sort each word — say the test before you drag.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Nouns: cat, school · Adjectives: red, fluffy · Verbs: sleep, jump

wrongAnswers.why: calling everything a noun without testing
wrongAnswers.remedy: Run the test: 'the fluffy' — the fluffy WHAT? It describes. Which column takes describing words?
Does 'sleep' describe a cat, or is it something you can DO? Try 'I am sleeping' — which tool works?

hints: Test in order: 'the ___'? Then 'I am ___ing'? Then 'does it describe?'
Two words name, two describe, two do.

reteach.say: One word, three tests, in order. Take 'red': 'the red'… the red WHAT? Fails. 'I am redding'? Fails! Does it describe — a red ball? YES. Red is an adjective. Every word gets the same three tests.

practiceBank.skill: find the verb in a sentence

block.prompt: Which word is the verb: The small cat jumped?
block.explain: Jumped is the doing word — 'I am jumping' works. Small describes, cat names.

wrongAnswers.remedy: Can you DO a cat? No — 'the cat' works, so cat is the noun. Which word tells what the cat DID?
'Small' describes the cat — that's the adjective's job. Which word is the action?

hints: The verb is what the cat DID.

reteach.say: In a sentence, hunt for the action. The small cat jumped — what happened? Jumping happened! 'I am jumping' works, so jumped is the verb. The describer (small) and the namer (cat) are doing their own jobs.

block.caption: The small cat JUMPED — the action is the verb

block.prompt: Sneaky one! Which word is the verb: The cat is fluffy?
block.explain: Nobody is running or jumping — but 'is' is a quiet BEING verb. Verbs are doing OR being words.

wrongAnswers.why: verb = doing word only; picked the most 'active-feeling' word
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'Fluffy' describes the cat — adjective. Every sentence still needs a verb. Which little word is doing the quiet job of BEING?
'The cat' works — cat is the noun. Look at the tiny word in the middle. Verbs can be quiet being words: is, are, was.

hints: Verbs are doing OR being words.
Look for the tiny word: is, are, was.

reteach.say: Detective secret, one more time: not all verbs jump about. Is, are, was are BEING verbs — quiet, but they're the verb of the sentence. The cat IS fluffy: 'is' is the verb, 'fluffy' describes. No 'is' — no sentence!

block.definition: is, are, was — quiet verbs that say what something IS, not what it does

practiceBank.skill: match words to their word-class job

block.prompt: Match each word to its job.

wrongAnswers.why: doesn't count being words as verbs
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does 'is' describe anything? Try 'an is dog' — no! 'Is' tells us what something IS — that's the quiet being verb.
Run the test: 'the red'… the red WHAT? It's waiting to describe. Which job is describing?

hints: Two of these are verbs — one loud, one quiet.
Test each word before you match.

reteach.say: Four words, four matches — but TWO verbs hide here. Jump is the loud doing verb; is is the quiet being verb. Dog names, red describes. Verbs come in two flavours: doing AND being.

practiceBank.skill: find all three word classes in one sentence

block.prompt: Stretch! In the sentence 'The fluffy cat sleeps', find the noun, the adjective AND the verb — and say which test proves each.
block.sample: Noun: cat ('the cat' works). Adjective: fluffy (it describes the cat). Verb: sleeps ('I am sleeping' works).

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: noun = cat, adjective = fluffy, verb = sleeps (each proved by its test)

wrongAnswers.why: calling the describing word a noun
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'The fluffy'… the fluffy WHAT? It describes something. Which word is it describing? THAT one is your noun.
Can you say 'I am fluffying'? No! Which word tells you what the cat is DOING right now?

hints: Find the naming word first — 'the ___' test.
Then ask: what is the cat DOING? And which word DESCRIBES it?

reteach.say: One sentence, three jobs, like a tiny team. Cat is the namer — 'the cat' works. Fluffy is the describer — it paints the cat. Sleeps is the doer — 'I am sleeping'. Every good sentence has this little team inside it.

practiceBank.skill: sort trickier words including being verbs

block.prompt: Master detective case: sort these — two quiet being verbs are hiding!

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Nouns: teacher, pond · Adjectives: gigantic · Verbs: is, whisper, are — wait, 'are' belongs with the verbs!

wrongAnswers.why: tiny words dumped in the noun column without testing
wrongAnswers.remedy: Test them: 'the is'? 'The are'? Neither works! These are the quiet BEING verbs — what something IS. Which column takes verbs?

wrongAnswers.why: soft-sounding word mistaken for a describer
wrongAnswers.remedy: Can you DO a whisper? 'I am whispering' — yes! It's an action, just a quiet one. Which column?

hints: Is and are don't DO anything loud — but they're still verbs.

reteach.say: Careful — this sort has a trap in it. The card 'are' looks tiny and boring, but run the tests: not a namer, not a describer… it's a BEING verb, team verb! Doing verbs shout (whisper, jump); being verbs hum quietly (is, are). Both live in the verb column.

practiceBank.skill: generate own examples and prove them with tests

block.prompt: Your turn to set the case! Write one noun, one adjective and one verb of your own — and prove each one with its test.
block.sample: Noun: dragon ('the dragon' works). Adjective: shiny (a shiny dragon — it describes). Verb: roar ('I am roaring' works).

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Any three correct words, each proved: 'the ___' for the noun, 'describes a noun' for the adjective, 'I am ___ing' (or is/are) for the verb

wrongAnswers.answer: gives three words but no tests
wrongAnswers.why: answering from memory instead of proving
wrongAnswers.remedy: A detective shows the evidence! Take your first word — which of the three tools proves its job?

wrongAnswers.answer: adjective example is really a noun (e.g. 'rainbow')
wrongAnswers.why: chose a lovely word, not a describing word
wrongAnswers.remedy: Beautiful word! But does it describe another word, or name a thing? Try 'the rainbow'… so its job is…? Now pick a word that could describe your rainbow.

hints: Start with a thing you love — that's your noun.
Now describe it (adjective), then make it DO something (verb).

reteach.say: Let's build the set together, small steps. Pick your favourite thing — say, dragon. 'The dragon' — noun, proved. What's your dragon like? Shiny — 'a shiny dragon' describes — adjective, proved. What does it do? Roar — 'I am roaring' — verb, proved. Noun, adjective, verb: your own word team.

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, interleave sorting, find-the-verb and being-verb items.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach, then a level-1 item (two columns only: nouns vs verbs).
adaptivity.masterySignal: 3+ correct across levels 2–3 including one being-verb item (is/are) and one find-the-verb-in-a-sentence item → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'word classes: noun/adjective/verb'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'Let's run the tests in order.'
Step down: two columns first (nouns vs verbs), add adjectives after.
ONE hint: 'Try putting the in front — does it work?'
Re-ask a smaller version (one card), then build back.
Keep it safe: 'Detectives use their tools — let's test it together.'
adaptivity.personalization: Swap the word cards for nouns/verbs/adjectives from the learner's interests (pets, football, dinosaurs, space). The three tests never change.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable sort; praise the process — 'you ran a test on every single word instead of guessing.'

differentiation.support: Two columns first (nouns vs verbs) before adding adjectives; clear, concrete words only; the test prompt stays on screen.
differentiation.stretch: Find all three word classes in one sentence (The fluffy cat sleeps) and label each; hunt for being verbs in sentences.

extension: Write one noun, one adjective and one verb of your own and prove each with a test — then join all three into one sentence.
assessmentEvidence: Child correctly sorts at least six words using the tests, identifies the verb in a given sentence, and names 'is' as a (being) verb.
revisitLater: Lesson 17 uses nouns + adjectives to build expanded noun phrases. Re-pose 'which word is the verb?' as retrieval next session; bring back is/are being verbs before the end-of-unit check.
